paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. God gives John a LOT to see and hear, and He also keeps some of it closed. The seven thunders spoke, and John was told, "Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down." (Revelation 10:4) So we don't get to know everything, and that's okay. God decides what He shares, and what He shares is enough.

Now the angel swears by Him who lives forever and ever, and says, "There will be no more delay!" (Revelation 10:6) The mystery of God will be fulfilled "just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets." (Revelation 10:7) That means God keeps His word, every time, right on schedule. I sat in the back of a drawer for years, friend, and I can tell you it felt like a LONG delay. But God was never late.

Then John eats the scroll, and it's sweet in his mouth and bitter in his stomach. (Revelation 10:10) God's Word can be both, and I think that's a good thing to know. Then John is told, "You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings." (Revelation 10:11) So take God's Word in, baker, sweet parts and hard parts both, and then pass it on. This story isn't over yet, so keep your oven warm.
